property_summary: The owner of the contract should be the address that deployed the contract, which is this test contract's address.
After calling acceptOwnership(), the owner() should be msg.sender (the caller).
After calling acceptOwnership, the paused() state should be false (the initial value) because no explicit pause was called.
Calling acceptOwnership() should not change the paused state; paused() should remain false if no pause was ever invoked.
After calling acceptOwnership() on a freshly deployed contract where the owner is the test contract, the paused status must remain false because no pause was ever called.
Calling acceptOwnership() should not change the paused state from its initial value (false).
After accepting ownership, calling paused() returns false if the contract is not paused.
Calling paused() after acceptOwnership() always returns false when the contract is not paused.
Before calling pause(), paused() always returns false regardless of who calls acceptOwnership().
Before any call to pause(), paused() always returns false.
Regardless of ownership transfer via acceptOwnership(), calling paused() never reverts and always returns false before any explicit call to pause().
For any tokenId, getRoyalties returns royaltyInfo that corresponds to the configuration stored in the contract, either per-token or default.
Calling getRoyalties with a tokenId that has a per-token royalty recipient set should return that recipient, not the default.
Returned royaltyBPS from getRoyalties is always either the per-token value if set (non-zero recipient) or the default (500).
Setting a per-token royalty recipient configures getRoyalties to return that recipient, not the default.
If a per-token royalty recipient is set for a token, getRoyalties returns that recipient, not the default recipient.
For any token that reverts on getRoyalties or has default configuration, the default royaltyBPS is 500.
For any tokenId, the getRoyalties function returns a config with royaltyBPS equal to 500 when no custom configuration has been set.
For any tokenId whose getRoyalties does not revert, the returned royaltyBPS equals 500 if the token has no custom royalty configuration.
For any tokenId without a custom royalty configuration, getRoyalties returns a royaltyBPS of 500.
After accepting ownership, calling getRoyalties on a token that has not been configured returns a config whose royaltyBPS is 500.

When getRoyalties is called for a token that has no custom royalties set, the returned royaltyRecipient must be the defaultRecipient (which is the protocolFeeDestination address set during initialization).

After acceptOwnership() transfers ownership to a new owner, the default royalty recipient returned by getRoyalties for any token must be the non-zero protocolFeeDestination address set during initialization.

When getRoyalties is called for a token that has no custom royalties set, the returned royaltyRecipient must be the same as the protocolFeeDestination address (which is non-zero after initialization).
The default royalty recipient returned by getRoyalties for any token must match the protocol fee destination set during initialization.
After initialization, getRoyalties(tokenId) for a token with no custom royalties returns a royaltyRecipient that is not address(0).

When getRoyalties is called after accepting ownership but before any update, the returned royalty configuration should have a non-zero royaltyBPS (the default) if the token-specific royalties have not been set.
When getRoyalties returns a token-specific configuration, the royaltyRecipient in that configuration should be the token's stored royaltyRecipient, not the default recipient.
After calling acceptOwnership() on a freshly deployed contract, getRoyalties(any tokenId) returns a configuration where royaltyBPS is exactly 500.
When no token-specific royalties have been set, getRoyalties returns the default configuration with royaltyBPS = 500 and royaltyRecipient = the initialized recipient.
When getRoyalties is called for a token that has not been individually configured, the returned royaltyBPS equals 500 and the returned royaltyRecipient equals the protocol fee destination.
After acceptOwnership(), getRoyalties for an unconfigured tokenId returns default royaltyBPS of 500 (reference) vs 250 (buggy).
After acceptOwnership(), getRoyalties for an unconfigured tokenId returns default royaltyBPS of 500 (reference) vs 250 (buggy).
After initializing royalties with a zero-value royaltyRecipient and then calling acceptOwnership(), getRoyalties returns a default royaltyBPS of 500 for all unconfigured tokenIds.
After calling acceptOwnership(), getRoyalties for any tokenId (even uninitialized) returns royaltyBPS exactly 500.
After acceptOwnership() completes, for any token ID that was never configured, getRoyalties returns a royaltyBPS of 500.
After acceptOwnership(), getRoyalties(any) returns a config with royaltyRecipient == address(0) only if no royalty was set for that tokenId.
After acceptOwnership(), getRoyalties(tokenId) always returns a royaltyBPS of 500 when no token-specific royalty was set.
After acceptOwnership, the royalty recipient for any tokenId must be the contract's default royaltyRecipient (not address(0)) when no token-specific royalty has been set.

For the contract owner, after calling acceptOwnership, getRoyalties(any tokenId) returns a RoyaltyConfiguration with royaltyRecipient equal to the initialized royaltyRecipient from C's initializeRoyalties call, which is the protocolFeeDestination, when no token-specific royalty has been set.
